name: Iowa
nameStory: Named for the Ioway people, who called themselves Baxoje. The shape to remember: Iowa is the only state whose entire eastern and western borders are both big navigable rivers - the Mississippi on one side, the Missouri on the other. It is a state held between two rivers.
capitalStory: Des Moines comes from the French 'Riviere des Moines,' which sounds like 'river of the monks' - and there were never any monks. The French were most likely mangling an Algonquian name for the Moingona people into words that made sense in French.

majorFeatures.name: Loess Hills
majorFeatures.note: Wind-blown silt bluffs above the Missouri

majorFeatures.name: Driftless Area
majorFeatures.note: Steep corner the glaciers never flattened

funFacts: Iowa has some of the richest topsoil on Earth, left behind by glaciers and windblown dust.
The Loess Hills are one of only two formations of their kind in the world; the other is in China.
Iowa produces roughly a third of all US pork.
Its northeast corner is 'Driftless' - the last glaciers missed it, so it kept its hills while the rest of the state got flattened.
